newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran proposed minister to lift wheat, sugar output.
newsitem.headline: Iran proposed minister to lift wheat, sugar output.

text.p: Iran's agriculture minister designate Issa Kalantari said if confirmed to his post he would work to raise Iran's sugar, wheat and other farm production.
Kalantari told the official news agency IRNA he plans to adopt programmes that would help raise wheat output to 14 million tonnes a year by the end of Iran's second development plan to the year 1999.

He said he would work towards raising sugar output to 1.4 million tonnes a year, vegetable oil to 200,000 tonnes, cotton to 700,000 tonnes, potato to six million tonnes, maize to 1.2 million tonnes and rough (paddy) rice to 1.9 million tonnes.
Kalantari was named in the proposed cabinet of President Mohammad Khatami. Parliament is due to start debating the nominations to the 22-member cabinet on Tuesday.
Kalantari predicted Iran's wheat output would exceed 10.5 million tonnes by the end of the Iranian year to March 1998.

He "expressed hope that under the new programmes and existence of suitable climatic conditions the annual wheat output would climb to 14 million tonnnes by the end of the second five-year economic development plan (1995-1999)".
Iran is expected to remain a major wheat importer in 1997/98 with the fourth position in the world league table.
Last month Iranian officials said Tehran would import five million tonnes of wheat this year in expectation its harvest would fall two million tonnes short of 12.6 million tonnes forecasts.
They said then that the wheat harvest in the Iranian year to March 1998 was not expected to exceed 10.5 million tonnes due to a drought which has caused extensive damage in some farm areas.

Kalantari said Iran's sugar-beet output is expected to rise to 6.5 million tonnes from 5.2 million tonnes, and the sugar obtained from sugar-beet and sugar-cane to 1.4 million tonnes from 850,000 tonnes by end of the second development plan.
Iran has bought increased steady amounts of both white and raw sugar throughout the year. It has said it was importing $100 million more sugar this year due to a fall in domestic output.
